CHIEF COMPLAINT
Positive hepatitis C antibody test

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents following positive hepatitis C antibody test identified during routine screening as part of recent physical examination. Patient reports feeling well and was surprised by the positive result. Denies any prior diagnosis or knowledge of hepatitis C.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports feeling well. No specific symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No other significant medical conditions. Recently completed physical examination.

MEDICATIONS
No medications.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Hypertension, diabetes, and depression.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Past history of intravenous drug use; patient has been clean for over 15 years. Alcohol use: Previously drank heavily; currently drinks beer daily but significantly less than before. Tobacco: Smokes 1-2 cigarettes per day; has decreased substantially but having difficulty quitting completely.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs reviewed and normal. General: No acute distress, no jaundice on skin. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm with 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. Pulmonary: Lungs clear without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. Abdomen: Bowel sounds present, soft, with splenomegaly noted. Extremities: No edema. Gait: Normal.

RESULTS
Hepatitis C antibody: Positive
Liver panel: AST 39 U/L (elevated); ALT, albumin, and total bilirubin within normal limits

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hepatitis C infection. Patient tested positive for hepatitis C antibody on routine screening. Discussed that hepatitis C is a viral infection of the liver; patient likely has had infection for several years with most patients remaining asymptomatic for years. Plan includes: (1) Confirmatory testing with HCV RNA and HCV genotype; (2) Assessment of liver disease severity with hepatic ultrasound elastography; (3) Family screening with HCV antibody test for wife and children; (4) Assist in coordinating family physician appointments for family screening; (5) Follow-up visit in 3 weeks based on test results to determine treatment approach; (6) Discussed importance of smoking cessation given hepatitis C diagnosis; will coordinate smoking cessation support with PCP if not already initiated.
